description:
The Allen Memorial Art Museum at Oberlin College was founded in 1917. Its Renaissance-inspired building, designed by Cass Gilbert, houses a teaching collection spanning many periods and cultures.

European and American painting and sculpture are complemented by Asian art, Japanese prints, ancient objects and other collections, connecting close study of individual works with a broad view of art history.

description:
The Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth brings a carefully selected art collection together with architecture by Louis I. Kahn and Renzo Piano. The original museum building opened in 1972, followed by the Piano pavilion in 2013.

Its collections range from ancient objects to twentieth-century art, including European painting and sculpture, Asian art, and works from the ancient Americas, Africa and Oceania.

description:
The Des Moines Art Center combines a museum, art school and sculpture park in Iowa’s capital. Established in 1948, its main campus includes buildings designed by Eliel Saarinen, I. M. Pei and Richard Meier.

A collection spanning several centuries supports exhibitions and learning, while studio classes and the Pappajohn Sculpture Park connect the museum with creative activity across the city.

description:
The McNay Art Museum in San Antonio grew from the collection, home and endowment left by artist and collector Marion Koogler McNay. It opened to the public in 1954 in her Spanish Colonial Revival house.

European and American painting, sculpture and works on paper form part of a wider collection that also includes theatre arts, art glass and work connected with New Mexico.
